headline: Gujarat's only hill country, forest, waterfalls and living adivasi culture in the Sahyadris.
overview:
Dang is unlike anywhere else in Gujarat: a small, almost entirely forested district folded into the northern Sahyadris, where the state's only hill station (Saputara) sits at nearly a thousand metres and the rain falls harder than anywhere else in Gujarat. Teak and bamboo forest covers most of the map, the Purna, Gira and Ambika rivers cut it into green valleys, and the population is overwhelmingly adivasi: Bhil, Kunbi, Warli and other communities whose festivals, crafts and village rhythms are as much the district's identity as its waterfalls.

For travellers, Dang splits naturally into three: the Saputara plateau with its lake, viewpoints and hotels; the Waghai belt at the foot of the ghat with Gira Falls, the botanical garden and Vansda National Park next door; and the interior, Girmal Falls, Don's meadows, Purna sanctuary and the Shabari Dham circuit, where distances stretch, mobile signal fades, and the forest takes over. Monsoon (July–September) is the district at full volume; October–February is green, cool and comfortable; summer stays kinder here than the plains below.

Dang rewards unhurried travel: fuel up at Ahwa or Waghai, carry cash, and let the ghat roads set the pace.

getting_there.road: From Gujarat: Surat–Bilimora–Waghai and up the ghat to Saputara (~160 km). From Maharashtra: Nashik–Vani–Hatgadh–Saputara (~80 km). Ahmedabad is ~400 km. State transport and private buses serve Saputara, Waghai and Ahwa; the ghat sections are winding but well surfaced.
getting_there.rail: Bilimora Jn (Mumbai–Ahmedabad line) is the practical railhead; the Bilimora–Waghai narrow-gauge heritage line runs limited services. Nashik Road station works for the Maharashtra approach.
getting_there.air: Surat (~160 km) and Nashik (~90 km) are the closest airports; Mumbai (~250 km) for wider connections.

local_transport: Shared jeeps are the true public transport of interior Dang, radiating from Ahwa and Waghai on market rhythms. Autos cover Saputara town; local taxis and sightseeing jeeps handle the standard circuits. App cabs do not operate here, arrange returns before heading into the interior, and expect no fuel pumps beyond Ahwa, Waghai and Saputara.

weather_by_month.notes: Cold, clear mornings on the plateau
Saputara's peak season, far cooler than the plains
Wettest weeks; waterfalls at full force

best_season: July–September for waterfalls and the monsoon spectacle (expect rain-interrupted plans); October–February for comfortable sightseeing, treks and wildlife; May for escaping the plains' heat at Saputara. March–April is the quiet, hazy low season.

emergency.police: 112 (national emergency); Saputara, Ahwa, Waghai and Subir police stations
emergency.forest_dept: Dang forest divisions, Ahwa; range offices at Mahal, Waghai and Subir handle sanctuary permits

tips: Fuel and cash exist only at Saputara, Ahwa and Waghai, plan the interior accordingly
BSNL and Jio survive furthest into the interior; assume dead zones beyond Ahwa
Monsoon driving means ghat fog and slow trucks: add buffer to every leg
Book forest campsites (Mahal, Kilad) via the official eco-tourism portal well ahead of winter weekends
Respect village norms when photographing, ask first, especially at festivals
